challenge.better_approach: I looked at keying the existing test_feedback.py (22 checks, no PROVES block) to the clauses. Its checks are one main() of check() calls, not teeth, so a clause cannot bind one by name. A new proof with one tooth per clause is smaller than restructuring that one.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a scratch root exercises the same code paths as the live corpus. Measured: every public function takes root, and the existing proof uses the same fixture shape.
challenge.prior_art: test_feedback.py covers most of the same ground as unnamed checks. f68bd50f2902 is the only ticket that names this charter, and it fixed Windows paths. 94e1cce8941e settled the probes ruling and does not touch these clauses.
challenge.real_collision: None. Clause 7's question is a spec choice, not a collision. Keep it and the build is in feedback's corpus_record; retire it and it is a charter edit. Either way it is Akien's.

answers.falsifier: Seven teeth green over feedback.py as it stands, and each reds under a hollow build of its own clause (why not required, a route that always resolves, a substring scan, proofs enrolled, a healthy entry that cannot be ==, an entry kept after the constructor goes, a default route). Clause 7 waits for Q#116.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator ruled the shape 2026-11-16 from the measurement that cairn/tools/feedback/intention+why.json was born in cairn 1ef9aa099 with no ticket, and intention_fidelity pairs it only with f68bd50f2902 (a Windows fix, invented 0.966)
answers.how: One proof under cairn/tools/feedback/proofs/ with a PROVES key per clause, each tooth running feedback's public functions over a scratch root. Clauses 1-6 and 8 hold and get teeth. Clause 7 does not hold as written (gate.proved accepts any keyword), so it is Q#116 at outline 17.10.1. No code changes.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (nothing in proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass) and Law 9 (red is the default): a charter born without a ticket has no proof bound to its own claims.
answers.what: feedback's charter is proved clause by clause: each of its falsifier's eight clauses gets one tooth against the code that stands, and a clause the code does not meet becomes a question to Akien.

bullets.text: feedback's charter gets a proof bound to its own falsifier; 7 of 8 clauses hold, and clause 7 is asked as Q#116.
